one_liner: MIT clean-room C++17 alpha wrapping (TOG 2022) without CGAL; about 2x faster than a GMP-free CGAL::alpha_wrap_3 build.
what_it_does: Turns an arbitrary triangle soup (open, self-intersecting, non-manifold, duplicated or flipped faces) into a watertight, outward-oriented, 2-manifold surface that strictly encloses the input, following Portaneri et al., 'Alpha Wrapping with an Offset' (ACM TOG 2022). Two knobs: alpha (carving-ball radius, so gaps and handles narrower than about alpha get bridged) and offset (how far outside the input the wrap sits). The C++ API is aw::alpha_wrap(std::vector<aw::Triangle>, alpha, offset, manifold, &stats) returning aw::Mesh{V, F}; there is also a CLI for OBJ/ASCII PLY and a nanobind Python module, alpha_wrap.wrap(V, F, alpha_rel=..., offset_rel=...). It is not a drop-in for CGAL: own mesh types, no CGAL concepts or named parameters, and no seeds or custom oracles (point sets, segment soups).
how_it_is_fast: It runs the paper's algorithm on its own data structures instead of CGAL's generic machinery: a roughly 1.2k-line incremental Bowyer-Watson 3D Delaunay on flat cell arrays with a free list, an enclosing super-tetrahedron instead of an infinite vertex, and Shewchuk's adaptive exact orient3d/insphere predicates (public domain). The input soup goes into a hand-written AABB tree that answers distance, closest point, tet-soup intersection and the offset-surface crossing; the crossing is found by sphere tracing the 1-Lipschitz distance field. Gates are flood-filled from a max-circumradius priority queue as in CGAL's sorted reference variant. The README attributes the measured gap partly to the comparison environment ('in this GMP-free CGAL environment'); no profiling breakdown is published.
when_to_use: Making watertight, manifold shells from defective meshes (scans, CAD exports, game assets, Thingi10K-style 3D-print models) for meshing, simulation, collision proxies or 3D printing, when you cannot ship GPL/LGPL CGAL code
Python pipelines that want a pip-installable wrapper over NumPy arrays (wheels are built for Linux, macOS arm64/x86_64 and Windows x86-64) without pulling Boost or CGAL

Coarse to medium wraps (alpha around diag/20 to diag/300) of meshes up to a few hundred thousand triangles: the README tested a 100k-triangle sphere and a 236k-triangle statue, and a 1000-model Thingi10K run gave median 1.1 s and p90 6.2 s per model
Batch jobs where a slightly coarser output (0.6-1.0x CGAL's face count) is acceptable or even preferred
when_not_to_use: When you need CGAL's exact output or its extra features (point-set and segment-soup oracles, seeds for interior wrapping, visitors, custom oracles, the faster unsorted LIFO queue): this implements only the triangle-soup path

When you already link CGAL with GMP: the only speed claim is against a CGAL 6.0.1 build with CGAL_DISABLE_GMP (Boost.Multiprecision fallback), with no timing table, hardware or compiler, so a normal GMP-backed CGAL may close the gap
Very fine wraps or huge inputs that need multithreading: the wrap is single-threaded (no threading in src/), and the Thingi10K worst case took 59 s on one model

Production code that needs a track record: the repo is two months old (first commit 2026-07-29, 8 commits, 10 stars, no issues filed), and the authors note a known residual degenerate case (zero-volume Delaunay cells) that is only detected, not fixed, by verify_topology()
Binary I/O or formats beyond OBJ and ASCII PLY through the CLI

integration.form: static lib (awcore, 4 .cpp files) plus CLI and Python wheel (nanobind, scikit-build-core)
integration.dependencies: Shewchuk's robust predicates (danshapero/predicates), fetched by CMake FetchContent from GIT_TAG master on first configure (network needed); NumPy for the Python package. Optional CGAL 6.0.1 + Boost 1.85 headers only for the reference tool or wrap_cgal (GPL-encumbered build).
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.16+; Python 3.8+ for bindings (wheels built for CPython 3.9-3.13); CI builds with Release on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest and windows-latest
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS (arm64 tested, x86_64 cross-built), Windows x86-64; no SIMD or architecture-specific code; musllinux, PyPy and 32-bit wheels are skipped
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each aw::AlphaWrap object holds its own Delaunay, oracle and labels, so separate instances on separate threads look independent, but no guarantee is stated
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same algorithm, guarantees and alpha/offset parameters as CGAL::alpha_wrap_3 for triangle soups, but a different API and mesh type, a slightly different (coarser) output, and no point-set/segment inputs or seeds

gotchas: Builds must keep -ffp-contract=off (set in CMake for GCC/Clang) and must not use fast-math, or the exact predicates break silently; vendoring the sources into another build needs the same flags

The flood fill stops at a hard cap of 5,000,000 Steiner points (max_steiner in alpha_wrap.cpp) and just breaks out of the loop; check WrapStats.steiner_points or the CLI's invariant report if you push alpha very small
The predicates dependency is fetched from an unpinned master branch, so builds are not reproducible and pick up upstream changes; pin GIT_TAG for production
Default CMake build type is RelWithDebInfo; the CGAL comparison used -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, so benchmark both in Release
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling does alpha wrapping. Pick it over Manifold or MeshLib when the input is a broken soup that their booleans reject or that you must first close: alpha-wrap is the repair/wrapping step that yields the closed manifold mesh those tools require, and it does so under MIT without CGAL. For booleans on already-clean meshes use Manifold, kigumi or trueform instead.
verified_claims_summary: The only speed claim is one README sentence: 'competitive to faster (ours ~2x faster on most inputs in this GMP-free CGAL environment)', measured by the author against CGAL 6.0.1 CGAL::alpha_wrap_3 with the EPICK kernel built header-only with CGAL_DISABLE_GMP, over the bundled meshes, a 100k-triangle sphere and a 236k-triangle statue at alpha = diag/30. No per-model times, hardware or compiler are given; output is 0.6-1.0x CGAL's face count and within 0.1-3.4% of the bbox diagonal (Hausdorff) of CGAL's wrap, so the two do not produce identical work.
status_note: Active but very new (8 commits from 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-31, every commit co-authored by Claude per the verifier), MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor; treat as a promising research-grade tool rather than a proven replacement for CGAL.
